verdict.rationale: Elicit ships a built-in Research Agent. Users hand it tasks in natural language, for example adding extraction columns, applying filters, exporting sources, generating figures and drafting slides, all inside the conversation. Effort levels and reusable skills let users shape how the agent works. Community reports criticize answer accuracy, but none show that delegation to the agent fails, so they lower confidence rather than create a dispute. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of the current Research Agent's task delegation, and evidence of how far it can carry multi-step tasks without supervision.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: filter and export your sources, save papers to your Library, generate figures, and draft slides, all without leaving the conversation
To add a column, simply tell the research agent what column(s) you'd like to add.
The simplest way to filter is to just say what you want in your Research Agent query. Elicit will automatically detect and apply the right filter.
A skill is a set of instructions you can hand to Elicit's agent so it approaches a task a particular way.
the Research Agent can pull from a wide range of sources (e.g. publications, public filings, press releases), produce flexible outputs, and let you iterate until you have exactly what you need
